target_name: Gross Financing Turnover Meets Cash Cover
rationale: The proposal's own reasoning concedes that six different first legs already produced near-identical results, which is direct evidence that the payoff comes from the IND_ZSCORE(oancf/at) leg acting through a strictly positive [0,1] rank weight — i.e. a re-labelled cash-based operating profitability signal (Ball et al.) — and the claimed coverage gain is dubious since nested ADDs of cash-flow items propagate missings rather than requiring "one non-missing flow."

target_name: Equity Base Turbulence Meets Cash Cover
rationale: This is an ABS() re-skin of the archive's existing "Dilution Intensity Meets Cash Cover" and, because the positive-rank weight cannot flip the sign of the cash leg, it cannot actually discriminate between the "engagement" and "dilution" mechanisms it claims to adjudicate — a univariate test of oancf/at alone would settle that question far more cleanly.

Multiplying two already-tested [0,1] rank weights onto the same cash z-score compresses the weight toward zero for most firms and shrinks coverage to the intersection of two sparse cash-flow overlaps, so it is a mechanical stacking of two prior signals rather than a new economic hypothesis, and the "reduced misclassification" claim is untestable given both legs enter as monotone weights on the identical conditioning variable.

This is the one proposal that perturbs the leg plausibly driving the entire family — swapping asset-scaled cash flow (which is close to the published cash-based profitability anomaly) for a cash margin that is roughly orthogonal to asset turnover — making it a genuine diagnostic of the industry/asset-intensity confound, though it remains a single-leg variant of an existing archive signal and oancf/sale will be unstable for low-sales firms even after winsorization.

Extending csho growth from one to three years is a re-windowing of the archive's existing best signal and the three-year share-count change is essentially the published composite/net share issuance anomaly, so neither leg contributes new information beyond what has already been evaluated.

Reframing external financing as a persistent state via TS_MAX is the most defensible of the within-family variants, but the weight is a lightly transformed version of the well-documented net external financing anomaly, the cash leg is unchanged, and the claim that coverage will broaden is unsupported because ADD(sstk, dltis) still requires both cash-flow items to be present.
